issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a Meal class (with constructor Meal(String, String[])) but the template repository provides an Order class with the same shape and leaves Meal.java empty. The solution repository implements Meal and does not include Order. This class-name mismatch across artifacts (Problem -> Meal, Template -> Order, Solution -> Meal) is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about which class to implement and use (the template's Main also references Order).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template consistent with the problem statement: provide a Meal.java matching the UML (Meal(String, String[])) and remove or rename the extraneous Order.java. Update the template Main (and any comments) to reference Meal instead of Order so students implement and use the Meal class as specified.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution refer to a conceptual entity named 'Meal', but the template repository provides an 'Order' class with the same structure while the template's Meal.java is empty. This mismatch (Meal vs Order) creates a direct mapping confusion: students reading the exercise expect to find and use a Meal class, but the starter code exposes Order instead, increasing extraneous cognitive load and risking incorrect implementations or wasted time searching for the expected class.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts: either rename the template's Order class to Meal (move/rename Order.java to Meal.java and update all references) and provide a populated Meal.java in the template, or update the problem statement to use 'Order' everywhere. Prefer renaming Order -> Meal in the template to match the problem statement and solution.
